sources.title: Hermes 3 - Llama-3.1 405B model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact Hermes 3 405B card explicitly identifies a full-parameter fine-tune of Llama 3.1 405B; YAML maps base_model to meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-405B. It documents ChatML, function calling and structured output, distinguishes a separate FP8 quantization, and retains license: llama3. It does not separately report an active-parameter count.

sources.title: Hermes 3 405B checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Pinned configuration freshly retrieved October 27, 2026: LlamaForCausalLM; 126 layers, hidden width 16384, FFN width 53248, 128 query heads, eight KV heads, untied embeddings, vocabulary 128256, BF16 and max_position_embeddings 131072. These core dimensions match the named Meta 405B base in its report. No expert routing, pruning specification, modality encoder or quantization configuration appears.

sources.title: Hermes 3 405B tokenizer and chat templates
sources.evidence: Exact 405B tokenizer defines paired SCRATCHPAD, REASONING, INNER_MONOLOGUE, PLAN, EXECUTION, REFLECTION, THINKING, SOLUTION, EXPLANATION and UNIT_TEST tokens in reserved IDs 128019-128038. These entries have special:false. Default ChatML and tool_use templates exist; model_max_length is 131072. No enforced thinking mode or reasoning-effort control appears.

sources.title: Hermes 3 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The August 15, 2024 author report announces available weights. Sections 2 and 4.1 explicitly map Hermes 3 405B to the 405-billion-parameter Llama 3.1 base with 131072-token context. Section 2.1 reuses reserved tokenizer IDs for reasoning tokens. The 405B retains its full-model SFT checkpoint; only 8B retained DPO. No structural compression or expansion is described. FP8 is evaluation quantization. The report does not separately publish active parameters.

sources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models, section 3.2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Section 3.2 and Table 3 describe the explicitly mapped standard dense Transformer with GQA. Its 405B column gives 126 layers, width 16384, FFN 53248, 128 query heads and eight KV heads, matching the exact Nous configuration. The report supplies nominal total size, not a separate active-parameter count.

sources.title: Llama 3.1 405B foundation model card
sources.evidence: The old Meta-Llama-3.1-405B base link redirects here. Identifies the foundation as an autoregressive Transformer, nominal 405B, text in/text out, 128K context and Llama 3.1 Community License. Its license text covers derivative works.

sources.title: Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Actual versioned license text for the explicitly identified base. Section 1 grants modification/derivative rights and requires distributing this agreement with Llama Materials or derivative works. This governing text is more specific than Nous metadata tag llama3.

sources.title: Unveiling Hermes 3: The First Full-Parameter Fine-Tuned Llama 3.1 405B Model is on Lambda’s Cloud
sources.evidence: Dated August 15, 2024, updated August 16. Explicitly announces partner Nous Research’s Hermes 3 405B launch and immediate public availability. Hosted deployment uses FP8. Its broader RLHF training statement conflicts with Nous’s 405B-specific SFT account and is not used for training claims.

sources.title: Freedom at the Frontier: Hermes 3
sources.evidence: Original announcement now displays August 2024 without a day. Identifies the 8B, 70B and 405B Llama 3.1 fine-tunes, internal-monologue and function-calling abilities, and offers access to Hermes 3 405B.

sources.title: Nous Research releases index
sources.evidence: Current retrospective index assigns August 24, 2024 to Hermes 3 405B and August 14 to the technical report. The later model date conflicts with the contemporaneous August 15 launch and author report; it is not used as earliest release evidence.

sources.title: Exact Hermes 3 405B repository file listing and metadata
sources.publisher: Nous Research / Hugging Face repository API
sources.evidence: Public repository lists 191 safetensors shards and eight non-weight files. No LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, LICENSE.md or NOTICE is present; each attempted raw URL returns 404. The only fine-tune license declaration found is card metadata llama3.

sources.title: Hermes 3 405B checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: Index lists 1137 .weight tensors for embeddings, head, norms and per-layer dense attention/MLP projections; no expert, router, scale or buffer entries. Only index/configuration metadata was read; no weight shards or tensor-header census was performed, and byte size is not treated as an exact learned-parameter count.

sources.title: Jamba: Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Models, ICLR 2025, Table 1
sources.evidence: Freshly downloaded and visually checked October 27, 2026. Table 1 on PDF page 5 explicitly lists Llama-3.1 405B with 405B available parameters and 405B active parameters. This establishes AI21’s nominal comparison convention for the exact named base, not a Nous or Meta active-count disclosure and not an exact per-token tensor census. Applying it to Hermes 3 is a labeled lineage inference supported by the original full-parameter fine-tune description, unchanged core dimensions and reuse of reserved tokens.

name.note: Existing display name accurately identifies the 405B instruct/chat fine-tune; official card heading is Hermes 3 - Llama-3.1 405B.

developer.note: Nous developed this fine-tune; Meta developed its foundation, and Lambda supplied compute/hosting.

family.note: Normalize the explicitly named Hermes series; nousresearch is the developer identifier.

release_date.note: Contemporaneous partner launch explicitly says available August 15. August 16 is its update date. The author report independently announces available weights on August 15; the current retrospective August 24 listing is later and conflicting.

open_weights.note: Author release states weights are available; public exact-model repository distributes safetensors shards.

license.note: The exact card explicitly identifies a Llama 3.1 405B derivative, whose actual license includes derivative works. Nous retains a legacy llama3 metadata tag and supplies no separate fine-tune license text; that tag does not replace the governing base agreement.

parameters_b.note: Fresh review retains the developer-published nominal 405B total for the explicitly named full-parameter Llama 3.1 405B fine-tune. The exact configuration and training report corroborate the lineage without structural compression or expansion. This is the original BF16 checkpoint, not its separate FP8 quantization; no tensor census, weight-shard download or storage-byte calculation was used.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal lineage inference under AI21’s published comparison convention: the Jamba ICLR 2025 Table 1 explicitly lists Llama-3.1 405B at 405B active parameters. Nous identifies this exact Hermes model as its full-parameter fine-tune; matching core dimensions, reserved-token reuse and the retained SFT checkpoint support transferring that nominal convention. This is not a direct Nous or Meta active-count disclosure, an exact count of participating tensors per token, or an inference from dense architecture alone. Exact per-token component participation remains unspecified.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Llama Transformer with grouped-query attention. The explicit foundation mapping and matching 405B configuration establish this without transferring 8B/70B specifications.

context_window.note: Exact configuration, tokenizer and report agree. The 8192-token supervised fine-tuning sequence length is not the model context ceiling; hosted limits may differ.

modalities.note: Causal text language model with text chat/tool formats; the checkpoint has no vision or audio components. Code is text output.

reasoning.note: Report documents training on structured reasoning/scratchpad tokens, independently present in this exact 405B tokenizer. This denotes trained structured traces, not an enforced API thinking mode, reasoning-effort setting or a claim about DeepHermes.

tool_call.note: Card documents trained tool-call/response syntax and the exact tokenizer includes a tool_use template. An external runtime parses calls and executes tools.

description.value: Nous Research’s 405B full-parameter fine-tune of Llama 3.1 for instruction following, multi-turn chat, structured reasoning, code generation, and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces the broad multilingual-chat assertion with capabilities directly documented for Hermes 3. The English-tagged fine-tune does not establish a validated multilingual support list merely by inheriting a multilingual base.

patch.description: Nous Research’s 405B full-parameter fine-tune of Llama 3.1 for instruction following, multi-turn chat, structured reasoning, code generation, and tool calling.
patch.notes: 405B is Nous’s nominal total. Nominal 405B active is inferred from the explicit Llama 3.1 405B full-parameter fine-tune lineage using AI21’s Jamba comparison table; it is not a direct Nous/Meta active-count disclosure or an exact per-token census. This record describes the original BF16 405B fine-tune, not the separate FP8 hosting checkpoint. Reasoning denotes trained structured reasoning/scratchpad tokens, without an enforced thinking-mode or effort control. The explicit Llama 3.1 base agreement covers derivatives; Nous’s card retains a legacy llama3 metadata tag and no separate license file. Earliest public launch is August 15, 2024; the current Nous retrospective index says August 24, conflicting with the contemporaneous launch.

sources.label: AI21 Jamba Table 1: base-model active-count convention

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit retains the nominal developer total of 405B and establishes nominal 405B active through explicit full-parameter Llama 3.1 405B lineage under AI21’s separately published active-count convention. Reopened Nous card/report, pinned config, Meta architecture report and original ICLR Table 1; no structural change defeats the nominal inference. Direct Nous/Meta active disclosure and exact per-token participation remain unestablished. The other twelve field assessments are unchanged.
